comparison: Perfect alignment on chemostat model findings (C8, C51, C54, C65, C66). Both evaluations support the resource-dependent diversity results from Figure 6. OpenEval notes model complexity makes comparison difficult; peer review acknowledges 'proliferation of parameters' but finds analyses sound.

Strong alignment on GC content findings (C7, C38, C39, C42, C61, C62). Both evaluations support the statistical results (p<0.05) and mechanistic interpretation linking GC content to dissociation probability. Peer review explicitly identifies this as a main result with 'intriguing' observations.

Strong agreement on error threshold mitigation (C6, C45, C46, C47). Both evaluations support mutation rate findings from Figure 4. Peer review emphasizes this as a key contribution showing parabolic growth 'mitigates the error threshold catastrophe.' OpenEval also covers C50 (reverse mutations) which peer review includes here.

Strong agreement on diversity maintenance findings (C4, C5, C31-C35). Both evaluations support quantitative simulation results from Figure 2. Peer review identifies this as the 'key result' with 'convincing evidence.' OpenEval notes model simplifications; peer review does not challenge these. Peer review also includes C3, C22, C23, C56 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Divergent evaluation types on evolutionary implications (C10, C71, C72). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting claims about parabolic growth being 'pivotal' or 'indispensable' cannot be evaluated from computational models alone. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable implications. Peer review also includes C9, C57 which OpenEval addresses in R12.

Divergent evaluation types on speculative proposals (C9, C57). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting extrapolation to periodic environmental fluctuations is not directly tested. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED within broader evolutionary implications (also covering C10, C71, C72), accepting these as reasonable without challenge.

Agreement on conceptual interpretation (C56, C75). Both evaluations support the connection to exploration-exploitation tradeoffs in evolutionary algorithms. OpenEval notes this is speculative application rather than tested result; peer review implicitly accepts as part of broader findings. OpenEval also includes C3 which peer review addresses in R1.

Agreement on literature-cited error rates (C68, C69, C70). Both evaluations support these as appropriately sourced estimates. OpenEval notes different experimental conditions; peer review accepts without critique. Peer review also includes C60 (population size threshold) which OpenEval addresses in R10.

Agreement on population size conclusions (C60). Both evaluations support this as valid inference from simulation results. OpenEval notes this is model-specific empirical observation; peer review accepts as direct inference without challenge. Peer review also covers C68-C70 which OpenEval addresses in R11.

Agreement on background claims about non-enzymatic replication and parabolic growth (C2, C13-C20, C29, C30). Both evaluations support these as well-documented properties with appropriate citations. Peer review groups these with other background claims (C1, C11, C12, C24, C25, C27, C58, C59, C63, C73) in a broader background evaluation.

Agreement on RNA world hypothesis background (C1, C11, C12). Both evaluations support these as well-established concepts with foundational literature. Peer review groups these with extensive other background claims in a single evaluation.

Agreement on theoretical challenges background (C24, C25, C27). Both evaluations support these as accurately representing known concerns in the field. Peer review groups these with other background claims; OpenEval also includes C26 which peer review addresses in R2.

Agreement on model implementation details (C28, C58, C59). Both evaluations support these as clearly stated assumptions based on known RNA properties. OpenEval provides separate evaluation; peer review groups C28 with methodological acceptance and C58, C59 with broader background claims in R7.

Agreement on miniribozyme and RNA folding background (C63, C73). Both evaluations support these as appropriately sourced literature providing context. Peer review groups these with other background claims in comprehensive background evaluation.

Agreement on reverse mutation analytical result (C50). Both evaluations support this as valid mathematical consequence shown in Appendix 1-figure 2. OpenEval notes biological relevance depends on back mutation rates; peer review includes this with error threshold findings without separate discussion.

Agreement on chemostat model mechanistic feature (C55). Both evaluations support the duplex stability affecting decay rates as logical model design. OpenEval provides separate evaluation noting model-dependent quantitative balance; peer review implicitly accepts this within broader GC content findings.
